posts.headline: 5 things your Google profile needs this week
points: Your real business name, nothing added
posts.caption:
5 things your Google profile needs this week

Your Google Business Profile is often the first thing a new customer sees, before your website, before your Instagram. It is free, and most local businesses leave half of it empty. Fix these five this week and you are ahead of most of your street.

1. Your real business name, nothing added
2. The most specific main category
3. Correct hours, holidays too
4. 10+ real photos
5. A reply to every review

posts.headline: Your website has 3 seconds

posts.caption:
Your website has 3 seconds

People on a phone decide fast. If they can't tell what you do, where, and how to reach you in about three seconds, they go back to Google and tap the next result. Open your own site on your phone right now and check those three things.

1. Say what you do and where, in one line
2. Phone number at the top, tap-to-call
3. One big button: Call, Book or Get a quote

posts.headline: How to ask for a review without feeling awkward
points: Ask right after a good moment
Send the direct link, not 'search us'
Ask every customer, not only happy ones
posts.caption:
How to ask for a review without feeling awkward

Most happy customers would leave a review. They just forget, or can't find where. Ask at the right moment, make it one tap, and ask everyone the same way. Rewards for reviews break Google's rules and the FTC's review rule, so keep it simple: just ask.

1. Ask right after a good moment
2. Send the direct link, not 'search us'
3. Ask every customer, not only happy ones
4. Never offer a reward

Reply to a bad review like this

A calm, kind reply to a bad review can win you more customers than a five-star one. The reply is not for the angry reviewer, it is for everyone reading later.

posts.headline: Why your website should load in under 3 seconds
points: Big photos are the usual problem
posts.caption:
Why your website should load in under 3 seconds

Slow pages lose visitors, especially on a phone with a weak signal. The fix is often simple: smaller images and fewer extras. Google's free PageSpeed Insights shows what slows you down.

1. Big photos are the usual problem
2. Shrink images before you upload
3. Fewer plugins and pop-ups
4. Test free with PageSpeed Insights

Questions? Ask in the comments and I'll answer.

posts.caption:
Don't stuff keywords into your business name

It is tempting to add keywords to your name on Google. It breaks Google's guidelines and can get your profile suspended. Your services, categories and description are where those words belong.

1. Use your real name, as on your sign
2. 'Best plumber in town' in the name can get you suspended
3. Put services in the Services section
